summary_out.next: The single-axis sweep is approaching exhaustion. L5 has two natural candidates: (i) one more single-step tightening to 7 ticks ($1.75) to confirm the lever has indeed exhausted (predicted endpoint: trade_count drops materially below base, pnl unchanged or slightly worse than L4) -- a clean diagnostic but low expected upside; or (ii) keep 5 ticks and ADD a structural conditioner on the admitted reversal -- the highest-leverage candidates are a hold-time floor (admit only if position is at least N seconds old AND has moved 5 ticks adversely), a spread-not-widened guard (skip override if current spread > 1 tick, since admitting reversals through wide spreads pays the mid-edge away), or signed aggressor imbalance on recent flow. Pick (ii) with the hold-time floor -- it directly addresses the failure mode that L1 (age-only at 5s) and L4 (adverse-only at 5 ticks) each individually under-perform base in ways that hint at compounding: age was wrong as the SOLE predicate (positions still mid-forecast at 5s), but at 5s AND 5-ticks-adverse the position has both matured AND been wrong, which is exactly the conjunction the base's blanket skip is too coarse to capture. Avoid: any return to single-axis age-only filters; any threshold below 5 ticks; abandoning the L1-L4 lineage.
